newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebels seen readying for two-pronged advance.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels seen readying for two-pronged advance.

text.p: Rebels who have captured a fifth of Zaire are now preparing for a two-pronged advance in Shaba region and the far north near the jungle home of President Mobutu Sese Seko, a regional military source said on Monday.

The source, who closely monitors Africa's latest war between Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) and Zaire's mercenary-backed army, said Shaba, a strategic copper- and cobalt-producing area, could fall within days.
"There is no doubt they are preparing for a rapid advance through Shaba. We have noticed a consolidation of forces in that area and the political climate seems to be in their favour," he said.
The ADFL, which launched its campaign in October, controls four towns in Shaba, an opposition hotbed and home to previous failed rebellions in Africa's third largest country.
The towns -- Kalemie, Moba, Manono and Pweto -- were all taken without a fight after government troops fled rising popular anger.

The source, who asked not to be named, said the ADFL was moving the bulk of its frontline fighting units from Kisangani, Zaire's third largest city seized on Saturday, on the route to town of Buta 260 km (160 miles) to the northwest.

Other rebel forces, buoyed by the capture of Kisangani -- a diamond- and gold-producing centre and the war's biggest prize so far -- were said to be moving to Buta from the town of Isiro, 320 km (200 miles) to the east.
Buta is seen as strategic by the rebels because it is the gateway to Mobutu's village and jungle palace at Gbadolite 440 km (270 miles) further on near the border with the Central African Republic.

"By moving to Buta and therefore knocking on the doors of Gbadolite, the rebels are challenging Mobutu's authority. The move has little or no military advantage, it is purely political," the source said.
Mobutu, in hospital in Monte Carlo for cancer treatment, has used Gbadolite as his command post and political headquarters for some 10 years.
The French Foreign Ministry said on Monday that Mobutu's health was "a source of concern" in the clearest indication so far that his condition had deteriorated.

Intelligence and military officials in Zambia, which shares a land and water border with Shaba, said they had noticed a sharp decline in Zaire's defence units in the area as scared soldiers retreated ahead of the rebel advance.
The rebels say they have moved to within 400 km (250 miles) of the Shaba's volatile capital Lubumbashi, a point confirmed by officials in Zambia.
